title: Coherent filtered Cartan--Eilenberg total pullback maps
statement: For every scheme $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and bounded-below complex $K$ of abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], there are simultaneously chosen termwise hypercohomology presentations $D(X,K)$ [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. Write $A_{X,K}=\operatorname{Tot}(I_{X,K})$ and $B_{X,K}=\operatorname{Tot}(\Gamma(X,I_{X,K}))$, extending resolution degree by zero and exchanging indices [def-sp-cartan-eilenberg-presentation, def-sp-double-complex-total]. There are spectral-sequence morphisms $M_{f,v}:D(X,K).\mathrm{sequence}\to D(Y,L).\mathrm{sequence}$ [def-sp-spectral-sequence] for every morphism $f:Y\to X$ and chain map $v:f^{-1}K\to L$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], whose first-page maps, under the signed identifications, are $H^p(v^q)\circ f^*$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. There are bounds $R(X,K,q,n)\in\mathbf Z$ and isomorphisms $e_{X,K,q,n,r}:E_r^{q,n-q}\cong \operatorname{gr}^q D(X,K).H_n$ whenever $r\geq1$ and $r\geq R(X,K,q,n)$ [def-sp-filtration]. For each $(f,v)$ there are a chain map $g:f^{-1}A_{X,K}\to D(Y,L).\rho.\mathrm{complex}$, a chain map $s:\Gamma(X,A_{X,K})\to\Gamma(Y,D(Y,L).\rho.\mathrm{complex})$, and an isomorphism $e:B_{X,K}\cong\Gamma(X,A_{X,K})$, satisfying: $f^{-1}(D(X,K).\mathrm{aug})\,g$ is homotopic to $v\,D(Y,L).\rho.\mathrm{map}$; in each degree $i$, $s^i$ is the global-sections inverse-image unit followed by $\Gamma(Y,g^i)$; and $e$ is the finite-diagonal comparison characterized by the following summand equation: for $m\in\mathbf N$, $k,n\in\mathbf Z$ with $m+k=n$, the $(m,k)$ diagonal inclusion followed by $e^n$ equals the extension identification for the $\Gamma(X,I^k)$ row, followed by $\Gamma(X,-)$ of the inverse extension identification for the $I^k$ row and its $(m,k)$ diagonal inclusion into $A_{X,K}$. For each integer $n$, there are maps $t_q:D(X,K).H_n^q\to D(Y,L).H_n^q$ whose composites with the filtration inclusions equal the source inclusions followed by $D(X,K).c_n^{-1}\,H^n(e\,s)\,e_{\rho_Y,n}$, where $e_{\rho_Y,n}$ is the canonical K-injective cohomology comparison [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. For every proof of compatibility of $t_q$ with the successive filtration inclusions, the stable-page map under the chosen $e_{X,K,q,n,r}$ is the induced cokernel map of $t_{q+1},t_q$, whenever $r$ is at least both source and target bounds. This construction asserts nothing about an arbitrary supplied lift between the two chosen K-injective resolutions.

proof.text: Shift a bounded-below complex so its terms below zero vanish. Apply the CE existence theorem and shift back. Use the first hypercohomology spectral-sequence theorem, with its signed row identifications and canonical resolution comparison, to build each presentation. Use the natural sheaf-H/derived-global-sections comparison on all rows, rather than separately chosen row isomorphisms.

The complex-degree filtration is top below a uniform lower bound b, but only degreewise zero at high indices. Crop it above an index c by replacing steps above c by zero; the result is a uniformly finite filtration of the whole complex. Apply the bounded filtered-complex spectral-sequence construction to these crops. For fixed total degree n choose c>n+1. The crop and original filtration agree in degrees n-1,n,n+1 at every index, so their cycle and boundary formulas agree on every page in bidegree (q,n-q). Increasing c gives identity filtered maps of the crops; canonical representative comparisons identify the maps with identities on the unchanged cycle/boundary quotients. Glue the page objects and structure maps through these identifications; choose one common c for the degrees involved in a differential or page-homology comparison. For a filtered map choose common lower and upper crop bounds in source and target, use naturality of the canonical representative comparisons, and glue the page maps. The page-zero graded complexes are those of the original filtration. This supplies simultaneous canonical choices, rather than unrelated choices of an objectwise spectral sequence.

Exact inverse image and the augmented CE comparison theorem give a bicomplex lift of every v. Totalize and follow by the target comparison to its chosen K-injective resolution to obtain g; the augmentation square gives its homotopy. Apply the global-sections unit degreewise to construct s. The finite-diagonal comparison supplies e with its specified summand equation.

The CE bicomplex map and global-sections unit preserve complex-degree filtration. Apply the canonical filtered spectral-sequence functor to obtain M for all chosen presentations. On each row the natural injective-resolution comparison computes cohomologyMap followed by H(v); the signed identifications use unchanged indices. This proves the first-page equation.

The image-filtration step maps are restrictions of the cohomology of this filtered total map. Transport their source along c_X and their target along the canonical resolution isomorphism to obtain t and ht. Finite tails in degrees n-1,n,n+1 make cycles and boundaries stationary. Choose a bound for each presentation and bidegree, and use the canonical quotient-to-image comparison at each later page for eInf. Naturality of the representative comparisons identifies the stable page map with the induced map on successive quotients, which is cokernel.map. The proof of the successive-inclusion square is irrelevant.
